title: Silt & Signal
page_copy: Carry Neri through seven living worlds to restore the old crossings. A cinematic hover-bike journey through cliff villages, broken aqueducts, midnight forests and sky orchards, with voiced scenes, music and water that reacts to the ride.
menus: Title/mode select (runtime-built buttons in the game frame): 'Begin the journey', 'Free ride & racing'

hud.note: No DOM gameplay HUD and no __getGameState; the game exposes __siltArcadeMode and __boot.

mechanic_notes: Cinematic hover-bike journey; seven worlds; restore old crossings; voiced scenes; water reacts to the ride.
limitations: No DOM gameplay HUD or game-state hook was observed after the start click; the post-start phase is inferred from the click sequence and an unchanged, settled scene (10,724 objects before and after), not from game state.
Object count is identical before and after the click in every run, so it cannot distinguish a menu scene from a gameplay scene; counts describe the single world scene.
Controls (W/S, A/D, E/Q) are declared by the plan/page copy, not runtime-verified (no fixed-input run; see R-25 part 2).

start_flow.note: Earlier diagnostic runs (cc1c9, cc1ca) first clicked 'Begin the journey'; the final run's first successful click was 'Free ride & racing'. Both are real buttons in the game frame.

root_cause_of_earlier_blocker: 'Timed out evaluating expression in child frame' was Prism's evaluate timeout, not a cross-origin block: the probe evaluates in the same about:srcdoc game frame successfully (median 8 ms) but a single evaluate can stall up to 4153 ms while the game loads under software GL (worst stall per run: 21 s at 1440x1000; 4.2, 9.2 and 16.8 s at 800x450). The pre-boot hook (context.addInitScript) reaches the srcdoc frame, so no child-frame session is needed.
